goal: The same screen recording, snappy: the pauses gone, the slow part sped up, the clicks punched in, captions on — the tutorial that respects your time.
audience: someone trying to learn the procedure
assumptions: the recording is a screen capture (the idle/freeze cuts and the punch-ins apply)
captions from the transcript where there is speech, UI labels where there is none
'snappy' means: no second where nothing happens
the input is one source: the named screen recording
no duration or format was named: the plan states its assumptions (the recording's own length trimmed tight, 16:9)

decision.why: Every ask is a measured edit: the pauses leave by the idle cut (freezedetect), the slow part by the speed op (audio locked), the click punch-ins by the overlay op on the transcript's click words, the captions by the caption design — one edit film, all four.

alternatives.rejected_because: the recording is the content — motion has no footage
the simplest thing that could work — and it is half the ask; the slow part and the clicks are named too

segments.brief: Ingest, transcribe, cut the idles (freezedetect), speed the slow stretch (atempo-locked), punch in on the clicks (the overlay op), captions throughout, one loudness.
acceptance: no frozen stretch beyond the max
cut pauses: the idle and silent stretches are removed
speed the slow part: the identified slow passage is sped up (audio locked)
the slow part is identified from the recording itself (the freeze/idle map)
zoom on clicks: punch-in zooms at the click moments
captions and zoomed content stay inside the safe area
snappy overall: the result is tight (a subjective row — the producer-critic judges it)

blocked_inputs: input:i1 — the screen recording does not exist (the human must supply it)

risks: a recording with no speech needs label-captions instead of transcript ones — the design covers both
